title: Fleet capacity fingerprinter and sparse warm-pool adjuster
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a lightweight fleet-level capacity fingerprint for short-term headroom prediction and a sparse warm-pool adjuster to reduce warmup costs while maintaining burst guarantees. Backwards compatible; no customer config required but opt-in tuning flags available for Dedicated customers.
description: Context: Dedicated fleets suffer occasional coordinated warmup costs when multiple tenants ramp simultaneously; autoscalers overprovision to avoid SLA blips. Motivation: reduce cost and transient latency by predicting short-term usable capacity and adjusting the warm-pool sparsity without weakening burst guarantees. What this PR does: 1) Adds a fleet-level capacity fingerprinter that ingests recent allocation events, per-pool occupancy histograms, and node provisioning latency to produce a lightweight short-horizon capacity fingerprint used by the autoscaler and admission controller. 2) Implements a sparse warm-pool adjuster that intentionally leaves a subset of warm slots in a probabilistic 'sparse' state and opportunistically pre-warms them when the fingerprint indicates pending demand. 3) Exposes telemetry and an opt-in tuning API for Dedicated customers to control warm-pool density and aggressiveness. Design notes: fingerprint is an exponential moving sketch (capacity/occupancy histograms with decay) stored per-fleet with configurable horizon (default 2m). The adjuster uses a conservative pre-warm policy to preserve the existing burst SLAs; when the fingerprint predicts >50% sustained headroom drawdown in the horizon, the adjuster transitions sparse slots to warm sequentially, bounded by a warm-rate cap. Safety: admitted capacity guarantees are unchanged; a short-lived burst fallback path was added to admission to use reserved cold slots (no impact to correctness). Rollout: feature gated for Dedicated clusters behind --enable-fleet-fingerprint and Opt-in flag in tenant config. Monitoring: new metrics (fleet.fingerprint.horizon_seconds, warmpool.sparse_fraction, warmpool.prewarm_rate, fingerprint.predicted_headroom_pct) and dashboards included. Testing: unit tests for sketch decay and adjuster logic; cluster integration tests with synthetic coordinated-ramp scenarios; canary rollout on two Dedicated pools for 48h. Impact: expected 6-12% reduction in warmup GPU-hours for typical multi-tenant patterns and 10-25% fewer transient latency SLO breaches during coordinated ramps. Related: builds on prior telemetry work (ENG-7123) and complements the warm-pool prewarm feature (ENG-7940).
commits_summary: 5 commits: initial fingerprint data model and API; sketch decay and ingestion worker; sparse warm-pool controller and admission hook; telemetry, dashboards and unit tests; canary rollout docs and feature gate wiring.
review_conversation: Owen Patel (reviewer): Can you explain why we chose an EM sketch vs full HDR histograms? Concerned about memory use for large fleets.

Author (Maya): EM sketch gives bounded memory and makes decay semantics explicit for short horizons. HDR would give more precision but is heavier; we profiled both and EM was ~6x lighter with comparable short-horizon accuracy in our traces.
Rita Gomez (reviewer): Need stronger safety net around admission path; if the adjuster prewarms too aggressively we should not evict lower-priority tenants.

Author: Added a prewarm_rate cap and tenant-priority-aware ordering; adjuster will never prewarm beyond reserved slow-path capacity. Added unit tests and a canary plan to monitor eviction-like events.
Noah Kaplan (reviewer): CI flaked once on integration test due to timing; please make the test less time-sensitive or add tolerances.
Author: Made test less timing-sensitive and replaced fixed sleeps with event-driven waits. Reran CI and green.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash. Canary monitored for 48h with no regressions; rollout flag enabled on two Dedicated regions, follow-up tickets created for gradual global rollout if telemetry matches expectations. Post-merge: created ENG-8410 for rollout automation and ENG-8411 for tenant-facing tuning docs.
